note: Built 2026-10-27 at ef9a5ce by reading the goal, requirements, status, roadmap, model, plans, open issues and pull requests, the code, and the systemd units on Brian's laptop. questions.question: Should the archive of 2,176 graphs get moves (how Brian argues) through the moves prompt live extraction now has behind a switch? No archive graph has moves today.
questions.blocks: any use of reasoning motifs or move sequences across conversations (tools/mine_motifs.py works only on the hand-built fixtures)
questions.resolves_with: A priority call, not a test: it costs a full re-extraction. The stop rule says no ontology expansion without a concrete product failure; moves are already in the ontology, so the question is only whether a consumer needs them.
questions.recommendation: Not now: no consumer needs moves today; revisit when a named use (for example 'how does Brian usually challenge a claim') is asked for.
questions.default: The archive stays without moves; the switch stays off.

questions.short: Reconcile the seed and review 858 records?
questions.question: Should the curated founding seed be reconciled against the full ChatGPT export and its 858 proposed annotations reviewed by a person (issue #3)?
questions.blocks: whether the seed can ever be called source-complete or confirmed, and depends on a fresh export reaching the laptop (issue #205)
questions.resolves_with: A priority call: only a person confirms records (ADR-004), so it costs Brian's review time; no argument settles whether that time is worth it.
questions.recommendation: Leave it unscheduled: the seed is a labelled curated fixture, the product value is the archive-wide positions memory, and nothing reads the seed as confirmed.
questions.default: The seed stays all proposed and labelled not source-complete; issue #3 stays open.

questions.question: Should the five-condition terminal-state reader benchmark (issue #225: does the corrected extractor improve an independent reader's resumption accuracy on the 2026-10-18 conversation) be run with live models?
questions.blocks: whether the 2026-10-18 extractor task and status corrections are judged by reader accuracy, and whether any schema change is considered for resumption
questions.resolves_with: Prior art and argument first: the roadmap forbids another benchmark without explicit approval, and the harness's own README says a schema change is considered only if existing elements cannot encode the terminal state, which the deterministic part already showed they can. A run would change one decision, whether to keep investing in resumption from graphs versus reading the raw tail; it is a single conversation, so it cannot generalize.
questions.recommendation: Do not run it now; the deterministic result already settles the schema question, and a one-conversation reader score would not change the roadmap.
questions.default: Issue #225 stays open and unrun; PR #218's protocol stays unmerged until someone needs it.

questions.short: Graph or archive search for answers?
questions.question: Should answers to cross-chat questions come from the graph route or from archive search then read?
questions.blocks: which route agents use for general answer retrieval
questions.evidence: Archive search then read is the default for that workload (0.67 against 0.63 and 0.61 key-point coverage), independently signed off; the graph is kept for attribution, open questions and history.

questions.short: Does the code execute typed rules?
questions.question: Does Inquiry Graph evaluate typed rules, so that its system model needs a metamodel mapped onto the shared kernel?
questions.blocks: system_model.executes_typed_rules and whether a metamodel is owed
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code and the metamodel reference settled it.
questions.evidence: No. Relations have named roles, but SIGNATURES only constrains which node kinds each role may bind and validate() checks shape (src/inquiry_graph/validate.py:67-82); no relation carries a formula, condition or effect that is evaluated, which is the trigger in bounded-design's typed-relational-metamodels reference. A kernel crosswalk exists as PR #15, kept unmerged on purpose.

questions.question: Are the adopted plans coding-sessions, report-relations-rescore and session-launch-kind finished, or still in progress under bounded-design@13?
questions.blocks: whether the stale recheck means re-adopting them under the current profile
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code and results settled it.
questions.evidence: All three are delivered: import-session and sessions are CLI commands (src/inquiry_graph/cli.py:64-68); headless launches are labelled automated (src/inquiry_graph/coding_session.py:31-35); the re-score is recorded (C2 0.62 against old C 0.63, evaluation/usefulness_pilot/results.md:74). Each plan lints PASS against its own adoption record. A finished plan keeps the method it was adopted under, so no re-adoption is needed; only the front-matter status is wrong (Q3).
